# Independent external CMap fixture

`japanese-cid.pdf` is generated by `generate.py` using ReportLab 4.4.9 with invariant output and uncompressed streams. It contains only the authored text `日本語の比較` (“Japanese comparison”) drawn with ReportLab's predefined `HeiseiMin-W3` CID font. No application/PDF.js code generates its bytes. It is original test material and may be distributed with this project.

SHA-256: `6ec499468b0f8f6900940e09a851903a20f2e0c16d5dc676bf2e520211792215`.

Regenerate with a Python environment containing ReportLab 4.4.9:

```
python3 test/fixtures/pdf-external-cmap/generate.py
```

The PDF contains `/Encoding /UniJIS-UCS2-H` and no `/ToUnicode`. Actual PDF.js 6.2.108 extraction requests both `UniJIS-UCS2-H.bcmap` and `Adobe-Japan1-UCS2.bcmap` from the packaged mapping assets (plus `LiberationSans-Regular.ttf`). Expected extracted text is exactly the string above, with no terminal newline.

`test/pdf-external-cmap.test.cjs` checks real production Node-child extraction and the real shared engine with instrumented local resources. `test/pdf-external-cmap-browser.cjs` uses the actual source browser adapter and a real module worker with in-memory local HTTP interception, without rebuilding the app. Both tests separately omit each required CMap, demand `DOCUMENT_RESOURCE` instead of degraded successful text, recover on the next extraction, and verify original bytes remain unchanged. The browser also rejects unexpected external requests.

This fixture qualifies predefined CMap loading. It does not establish support for all CJK fonts, vertical writing, OCR, or reading-order inference.
